summary: The code is syntactically valid and has a reasonable modular skeleton (data loading, network, exposure, policy, diffusion, decision, retail, aggregation). However, it does not implement or execute the actual simulation loop, calibration, predictions, or evaluation. The main() function is empty and the intended main() call is mistakenly inside a docstring, so nothing runs. Several critical requirements from the task are missing.

issues.description: Simulation core is missing. The Simulation.run method is empty (only a docstring) and there is no discrete-time loop executing modules, updating states, or collecting results.
issues.solution: Implement the run() method: iterate over days, compute policy/media signals, exposures, information diffusion, retail purchases, mask adoption, aggregate outcomes, and store daily results over training and validation periods.

issues.description: main() is a no-op and nothing triggers the simulation. The intended global call to main() is embedded in a docstring and is not executed.
issues.location: top-level main() definition and the final lines of the file
issues.solution: Implement main() to construct Simulation(MODEL_PLAN), call initialize(), run(), and print or save evaluation results. Move the global call `main()` out of the docstring so it executes at import time as required by the sandbox.

issues.description: The final main() call is inside the docstring for Simulation.run, so it is treated as a string literal and is not executed. This also violates the special requirement to directly call main() at global scope.
issues.location: End of file: lines after `def run(self) -> None:`
issues.solution:
Close the docstring properly and place `# Execute main for both direct execution and sandbox wrapper invocation
main()` outside any string literal at the global scope.

issues.description: No calibration step implemented. The task specifies calibration (e.g., CMA-ES) on training data; code lacks any optimizer or parameter fitting routine.
issues.solution: Add a calibration routine (e.g., using pycma or a custom CMA-ES/alternative optimizer) to minimize RMSE_adoption over the training window by tuning selected parameters, respecting bounds and convergence tolerance.

issues.description: No evaluation metrics calculation against observed data and no out-of-sample predictions for days 30-39. Metrics like RMSE, MAE, peak, time_to_50_percent, final_adoption, and inequality gini are defined but never computed.
issues.solution: After running the simulation, compute daily adoption series, compare to observed data to compute RMSE/MAE for training and validation, and compute peak, time_to_50_percent, final_adoption, and adoption_inequality_gini using provided Metrics utilities.

issues.description: Information from train_data.csv is not used beyond day 0 initialization; there is no fitting or validation against this data across days 0-29 and 30-39.
issues.location: Simulation.initialize (partial) and missing use in run()
issues.solution: Use train_data to compute observed daily adoption rates over the training and validation windows, then evaluate the simulated series against them.

issues.description: Validation criteria (goodness-of-fit threshold, convergence criterion, parameter bounds, out-of-sample validation) are not implemented.
issues.solution: Implement checks: enforce parameter bounds during calibration, stop when improvement < tolerance, verify RMSE threshold, and assess MAE on validation period.

issues.description: Retail and inventory logic does not decrement inventory when masks are worn and does not deduct budgets on purchase, which can invalidate the inventory constraint and economic effects.
issues.location: RetailMarket.step and MaskAdoptionDecision usage of mask_inventory
issues.solution: Deduct price from buyer budgets on purchase, track daily consumption (reduce inventory for agents wearing a mask), and possibly limit purchases to affordability and stock.

issues.description: AdoptionAggregator adds observation noise to the adoption rate that could affect evaluation if used directly.
issues.solution: Use `adoption_rate_true` for metric comparisons and reserve `adoption_rate_daily` (noisy) for simulated observation outputs if needed.

issues.description: ExposureCalculator loops over agents for each layer and recomputes neighbor index lists daily; for large N this may be slow.
issues.solution: Precompute neighbor index arrays once and reuse; vectorize where possible.

issues.description: Optional imports networkx and matplotlib are unused.
issues.solution: Remove unused imports or leave as optional only if planned for future diagnostics.
